title: Issue: Assigning Serial Numbers to Existing Stock without Increasing Qty

posts.name: Dharam Kumar
posts.cooked:
ERPNext Version: V15
Modules Affected: Stock / Inventory / Serial No

Scenario:

I have existing stock of some items (X: 100 qty, Y: 50 qty) that are already used in transactions like Sales Orders, Delivery Notes etc.
However, these items did not have Serial Numbers assigned at the time of stock entry.

Recently, I updated these items to set has_serial_no = 1.

Now, I want to assign Serial Numbers to this already existing stock without changing the actual quantity, and I have a list of Serial Numbers (from Excel) like:

X: SN1 to SN10
Y: SN11 to SN15

What I’ve Tried:

  1. Stock Reconciliation –
    Assigned serial numbers through reconciliation, but it increased the stock quantity which is not acceptable.
  2. Material Receipt –
    Added serial numbers with MR, but again it increased quantity.
  3. Repack Entry –
    Tried repacking to replace non-serial with serial items, but faced the same qty duplication issue.
  4. Manual SQL Insert into tabSerial No–
    This allowed me to insert Serial Numbers and link to items, but:
  • Actual stock qty is reset to -2
    When creating DN with 2 serials, actual qty goes -2.

My Goal:

Assign serial numbers to existing stock items without modifying actual stock quantity, and continue using serial-based tracking for future DN/SO.

What’s the Best Practice for This Use Case?

  • Is there any clean ERPNext-supported method (e.g. Repack with correct config, Custom Script, Backend patch, or Manual stock ledger entry) to do this without qty mismatch?
  • Or should I write a script that creates valid Serial No records and updates stock ledger entries accordingly?

Additional Notes:

  • I am open to custom scripting if needed.
  • Happy to share the Excel file or video if required.

Let me know the best way to approach this scenario.

Thanks in advance!

posts.name: Ahsan Tareen
posts.cooked:
Hi @dkumar

Once a stock item has had stock transactions (like Purchase Receipts, Stock Entries, or Sales Invoices), you cannot directly enable serialization (i.e., check the “Has Serial No” checkbox) for that item. This is because serialized items require ERPNext to track each unit individually via serial numbers, and any prior transactions without serial numbers break this consistency.

On the other hand if you can;

  • Manually update the item via SQL or system/developer console to check “Has Serial No”.
  • Then manually assign serial numbers via Stock Ledger/Serial No Tool.

However this method;

  • Can break your ledger if not done precisely.
  • Is unsupported by ERPNext as there are multiple records which needs to be updated.

The Solution is to use a new item or other wise recall all transaction and then mark Has Serial checkbox on and continue.
